contraindications: Potential difficulty or frustration due to the persistent and distracting nature of the thinking self's commentary.
original_extraction.evidence_text:
Hopefully, during that exercise you experienced that awareness of the body is very different from
thinking about it. The thoughts you had while you did the exercise came from your thinking self.
But the awareness of your body—the noticing of the different sensations, urges, movements and
positions—came from your observing self.

---

If you didn’t experience this distinction, do the above exercise again. And notice that while the
thinking self is talking away, the observing self is simply paying attention to your body. Notice, too,
that there are brief moments (which may last less than a second) when the thinking self shuts up and
the observing self can observe without any distraction.

---

Once you have experienced that distinction, it’s time to move on to...

---

In practising expansion, we need to sidestep the thinking self—to put aside its unhelpful comments
—and connect with our emotions through the observing self. This enables us to experience our
emotions directly, to see them as they actually are, rather than as the thinking self says they are.
According to the thinking self, ‘negative’ emotions are giant, dangerous demons, but the observing
self reveals them for what they are: relatively small and harmless.

---

So in practising expansion, the aim is to observe your emotions, not to think about them. There’s
just one problem: the thinking self never shuts up! (At least, not for more than a few seconds at a
time.) This means that while you practise expansion, your thinking self will continually try to
distract you. It may pass judgements on your feelings or try to analyse them, or tell you scary
stories about them or claim that you can’t handle them, or insist that it’s all too hard. Or it may say,
‘Don’t bother with these exercises; reading about them is enough.’ It may even suggest that you ‘do
them later’, knowing full well that you probably won’t.
generation_rules: Encourage repeated practice of body awareness exercises to experience the distinction between thinking self and observing self.
Sidestep or put aside unhelpful comments from the thinking self during expansion practice.
Focus on observing emotions directly rather than thinking about them.
pause_rules: Notice brief moments when the thinking self is silent to allow undistracted observation by the observing self.
original_extraction.psychological_function: Promotes awareness and acceptance of emotions by reducing judgmental and analytical interference from the thinking self, allowing emotions to be seen as less threatening.
repetition_rules: If the distinction between thinking self and observing self is not experienced, repeat the exercise.
Recognize that the thinking self rarely shuts up for more than a few seconds, implying the need for ongoing practice.
symbolic_elements: negative emotions as giant, dangerous demons
observing self revealing emotions as small and harmless
original_extraction.therapeutic_function: Facilitates differentiation between the observing self and the thinking self to enable direct experience of bodily sensations and emotions without cognitive interference.
voice_rules: Use language that distinguishes the thinking self as talkative and judgmental and the observing self as quiet and attentive.
Acknowledge the persistent nature of the thinking self's distractions.
